meaning_ledger.fact: Live dots flow along the lines, direction = traffic direction (historical line 5)
meaning_ledger.how: `flow: true`, `dots: 1` on every edge; direction follows each audited from -> to

meaning_ledger.fact: Motion speed should represent an indicated speed (historical line 5 wish)
meaning_ledger.reason: Fixed constraint: motion speed must not be a measurement. Every route runs the same 2000 ms shared clock, so no dot speed encodes 1/10/25 GbE. Link speeds stay in the edge labels only.

meaning_ledger.how: `dots: 1` gives exactly one dot per route (sparse); the shared 2000 ms default is the whole cycle per route (slow). The source gives no numeric rate, so no per-edge `duration_ms` override is written.

meaning_ledger.fact: Node boxes should share one background so borders render smoothly; no dots behind the drawing (historical line 5)
meaning_ledger.reason: Renderer chrome, not a graph fact: the spec has no field for node fill or for background dots, and the frozen binary's viewer already paints the flat box/background style. Asserting it in the spec would mean inventing a capability.

meaning_ledger.fact: The visualise pane should be an even split (historical line 48)
meaning_ledger.reason: A pane/composition requirement, not a relationship. The evidence capture did split at ratio 0.5 (half pane, 77x47 measured).

meaning_ledger.fact: Preserve core->cache and web->cache as separate relations
meaning_ledger.how: Two distinct edges in two views (e4 in v1, e5 in v2); no trunk, no merge

meaning_ledger.fact: Keep 1 GbE, 10 GbE and 25 GbE visible without implying motion speed is a measurement
meaning_ledger.how: Every speed is an edge label; all motion shares one synchronized duration

layout_attempts.note: No source group, layer order or tier band was reordered in any attempt; no relation was merged and no label dropped.

known_defects.detail: The 2-hop web -> db route leaves the Web tier beside the web -> Redis route and bridges it (`⌒` glyph in the capture) before passing the Redis band. Both tb and lr layouts report 1, because two edges leave one node toward the same side while a third link (cache -> db) sits between them. Not removable without reordering the tiers or dropping a relation, which the protocol forbids.

known_defects.defect: no single view carries the whole network
known_defects.detail: 6 nodes / 7 edges in one drawing needs 6 layers: 40x48 (tb) or 144x20 (lr) at natural zoom. The honest resolution was a two-view split with an explicit coverage map; a judge that requires one self-contained graph will see this as a gap.

known_defects.defect: harness pane capture starts at frame 1
known_defects.detail: scripts/viz-evidence.sh --frames 21 captures frames 1-20 in v*-frames.txt (frame 0 is not in the pane scrollback window; reproduced twice, so it is not a race). Frame 0 evidence therefore comes from the frozen binary run directly at COLUMNS=77 LINES=47 in frames/<view>-direct-frames.txt, which is deterministic output of the same binary and spec.

known_defects.defect: arrival frame shows no visible dot
known_defects.detail: At 2000 ms every dot is absorbed by its arrowhead glyph (documented round-03 renderer behaviour for a synchronized single-dot route), so frame 20 shows the finished drawing with no dot. Origin (frame 0) and synchronous progress (frames 1-19) are the motion proof.

`herdr pane layout` reports only the workspace-focused tab, and this worktree session runs in a background tab, so the script's rect lookup returned nothing. Rows come from the pane viewport (47) and the size proof is the app's own header token `77x47 @100%`.

known_defects.defect: case root is not itself a validation bundle
known_defects.detail: The literal command `python3 scripts/viz-validate.py docs/visualize-eval/rounds/03/network --require-select --require-frames --attempts .../attempts.json` fails manifest_readable because manifests live per view under evidence/<view> (see validate-case-root.txt). The per-bundle commands both pass.
